title: NTA UGC NET English Full Mock Test #18
subtitle: 100 Questions · 200 Marks · Post-2018 NTA Pattern · Zero Answer Bias (25 A/B/C/D) · Reading Comprehension (Q91-100)

items.title: Mock #18 · Q1
items.stem:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Work):
A. Lions and Shadows
B. The Still Centre
C. Translation of Agamemnon
D. The Sea and the Mirror

List II (Author):
I. W. H. Auden
II. Louis MacNeice
III. Stephen Spender
IV. Christopher Isherwood

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Lions and Shadows (1938, A) is an autobiographical novel by Christopher Isherwood (IV), The Still Centre (1939, B) is a poetry collection by Stephen Spender (III), the verse translation of Aeschylus's Agamemnon (1936, C) is by Louis MacNeice (II), and The Sea and the Mirror (1944, D) is by W.H. Auden (I).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q2
items.stem: In Biographia Literaria S.T. Coleridge defines the imagination as the faculty by which
options: the soul perceives the phenomenal diversity of the universe
the mind acquires images by its associative power
the soul perceives the spiritual unity of the universe
the mind separates images by its discriminatory power.
items.explanation: In Biographia Literaria (1817), Samuel Taylor Coleridge defines the imagination (esemplastic power) as the vital, synthetic faculty by which the soul perceives the underlying spiritual unity of the universe, in contrast to 'fancy', which merely associates and rearranges separate sensory images.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q3
items.stem:
Which of the following are plays written by Harold Pinter?
A. Family Voices
B. A Moon for the Misbegotten
C. The Room
D. No Man's Land
E. Krapp's Last Tape
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Family Voices (1981, A), The Room (1957, C), and No Man's Land (1975, D) are plays written by British dramatist Harold Pinter. A Moon for the Misbegotten (1947) is by Eugene O'Neill, and Krapp's Last Tape (1958) is by Samuel Beckett.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q4
items.stem: Who among the following is said to have believed that the Persian Gulf War (1990-91) never happened?
items.explanation: French postmodern theorist Jean Baudrillard published three provocative essays collected as The Gulf War Did Not Take Place (La Guerre du Golfe n'a pas eu lieu, 1991), arguing that the 1990–91 conflict was a televised media simulacrum.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q5
items.stem:
Arrange the following works of V.S. Naipaul in the chronological sequence:
A. A House for Mr. Biswas
B. The Mimic Men
C. The Mystic Masseur
D. Half A Life
E. Magic Seeds

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The chronological sequence of works by V.S. Naipaul is: The Mystic Masseur (1957, C); A House for Mr. Biswas (1961, A); The Mimic Men (1967, B); Half a Life (2001, D); and Magic Seeds (2004, E).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q6
items.stem: In the area of theory and research known as Second Language Acquisition (SLA), the classroom is considered
options: a site that always produces language learning blockade.
items.explanation: In Second Language Acquisition (SLA) theory and pedagogy (such as David Nunan's and Rod Ellis's classroom research), the language classroom is viewed as an 'experimental laboratory' where instructional hypotheses and learner interactions can be systematically observed and tested.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q7
items.stem:
Assertion (A) :
Our reality is linguistic, a language mediated reality.
Reason (R)     :
Our perception and understanding of reality are largely constructed by the
words and other signs we use.
In the light of the statements above,
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
items.explanation: In structuralist and poststructuralist theory, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) directly explains (A): human reality is linguistically mediated precisely because our concepts, categories, and perceptions of the world are constructed through language and sign systems.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q8
items.stem:
In medieval England a __________was understood to be a trained craftsman, one who
worked under a master who owned the business.
items.explanation: Under the medieval English guild hierarchy, a journeyman was a qualified craftsman who had completed his apprenticeship and was paid daily wages to work under an established master artisan before earning the status to run his own business.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q9
items.stem:
Which among the following are not true about The Defense of Poesie by Philip Sidney?

A. The text was published posthumously in 1595

B. Its also titled as An Apology for Poetry

C. Philip Sidney criticises Geoffrey Chaucer's Troilus and Criseyde and Spenser's The Shepheardes Calendar

D. The text is the first major piece of literary criticism in English

E. The text defends Plato for his decision to ban poets from the ideal state as described in Republic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Statements C and E are not true: Sir Philip Sidney actually praises Chaucer's Troilus and Criseyde and Spenser's The Shepheardes Calender, and he refutes rather than defends Plato's banishment of poets from the ideal commonwealth. Statements A, B, and D are historically true of The Defence of Poesie (1595).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q10
items.stem: The book Women Beware Women was published in the year
items.explanation: Thomas Middleton's Jacobean tragedy Women Beware Women is dated by dramatic historians to c. 1621 (though first printed posthumously in Two New Playes in 1657).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q11
items.stem:
Match the column:
A. Cynthia’s Revels
B. The Maid’s Tragedy
C. Women Beware Women
D. The Shoemakers’ Holiday
I. Thomas Middleton
II. Ben Jonson
III. Thomas Dekker
IV. Beaumont and Fletcher
items.explanation: These Early Modern English dramas match their playwrights: Ben Jonson wrote the satirical court comedy *Cynthia's Revels* (A-II, 1600), Francis Beaumont and John Fletcher co-authored the tragedy *The Maid's Tragedy* (B-IV, c. 1610), Thomas Middleton authored the Jacobean revenge tragedy *Women Beware Women* (C-I, c. 1621), and Thomas Dekker wrote the citizen comedy *The Shoemaker's Holiday* (D-III, 1599).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q12
items.stem: Who among the following in the article, "Fleshly School of Poetry", attacked the Pre-Raphaelites, especially D. G. Rossetti?
items.explanation: Scottish poet and critic Robert Williams Buchanan published the polemical article 'The Fleshly School of Poetry' in The Contemporary Review (October 1871) under the pseudonym Thomas Maitland, attacking Dante Gabriel Rossetti and the Pre-Raphaelites for sensualism.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q13
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are true about ‘cyberfeminism’?
(A) Women are not demanding material and social space
(B) Itinterrogates the patriarchal nature of the new Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
(C) It is a negotiation with the contemporary culture’s extensive informatization
(D) Virtual environment does not provide greater freedom to women
(E) Women are unable to appropriate the maternality of cyberspace
items.explanation: Cyberfeminism interrogates how patriarchal structures operate within information and communication technologies (B) and critically negotiates contemporary society's pervasive informatization (C). Statements A, D, and E are incorrect because cyberfeminists actively claim online spaces and view virtual environments as liberating for women.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q14
items.stem:
The arrival of printing in fifteenth
century England was engineered
by
items.explanation: English merchant, diplomat, and translator William Caxton introduced the printing press to England at Westminster in 1476, printing landmark Middle English works including Chaucer's The Canterbury Tales and Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q15
items.stem:
What is the correct sequence of various periods of English Literature?
A. Caroline Age
B. Jacobean Age
C. Restoration Age
D. Commonwealth Period
E. Augustan Age
items.explanation: The historical sequence of English literary eras is: Jacobean Age (1603–1625), Caroline Age (1625–1649), Commonwealth Period (1649–1660), Restoration Age (1660–1700), and Augustan Age (1700–1745). This gives the sequence B, A, D, C, E.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q16
items.stem: Which of the following is not correct about tribal narratives and the writers?
options: Escaping the Land is written by Mamang Dai
Amrutara Sanatana is written by Pratibha Ray
Motherland Being Deserted is written by Salge Hansda
items.explanation: Amrutara Santana (The Sons of the Soil / Dynasty of the Immortals, 1947), a celebrated Odia novel depicting the Kondh tribal community, was written by Gopinath Mohanty, not Pratibha Ray. Escaping the Land is by Mamang Dai and Kocharethi: The Araya Woman is by Narayan.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q17
items.stem:
Given below are two statements—one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R) :
Assertion (A) : The dialects of English that have resulted from the regional separation of English-speaking communities have not acquired the status of languages.
Reason (R) : The Germanic dialects that are now Dutch, English, German, Swedish etc., have become distinct owing to geographical dispersion.
In the light of the above two statements choose the correct option :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
items.explanation: Both statements are true, but the Germanic dispersion is a different case. It does not explain why English dialects stay dialects.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q18
items.stem:
Which of the following statements is
NOT TRUE of Dante Gabriel Rossetti ?
options: Rossetti was a Londoner, the son of an Italian refugee who taught Italian at King's college
Rossetti formed the Pre- Raphaelite Brotherhood with Holman Hunt, Ford Madox Brown and Painter Millais
He married Christina Georgina who was a poet in her right
Rossetti's "Blessed Damozel" displays his remarkable gifts as a poet and painter
items.explanation: Christina Georgina Rossetti (1830–1894), the celebrated poet of Goblin Market, was Dante Gabriel Rossetti's younger sister, not his wife. Dante Gabriel Rossetti married the Pre-Raphaelite model and artist Elizabeth Siddal in 1860.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q19
items.stem:
Globalization is antithetical to :
(A) The movement of capital
(B) The movement of commodities
(C) Cultural nationalism
(D) People
(E) Narcissism
items.explanation: Globalization promotes transnational capital, goods, and cross-border migration, but it is antithetical to closed cultural nationalism (C) and insular narcissism (E) by fostering global interdependence and eroding parochial borders.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q20
items.stem: Identify the one erroneous statement on Neoclassicism listed below :
options: Lodovico Castelvetro and Torquato Tasso reatly influenced English writers like Milton and Dryden.
The English relation to Neoclassicism was one of dialogue. Most literally, this dialogue is effected in Addison’s An Essay on Dramatic Poesy.
Boilean’s L’Art poétique influenced Pope’s Essay on Criticism.
Neoclassicism took its final form during the reign of Louis XIV (1638-1715).
items.explanation: Statement (4) is erroneous because An Essay of Dramatic Poesy (1668) was written by John Dryden, not Joseph Addison; Addison was an Augustan essayist associated with The Tatler and The Spectator.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q21
items.stem:
Match List I with List II
List I (Authors) – List II (Works)
(a) Ferdinand de Saussure  (i) “Two Aspects of language and two types of Aphasic Disturbances”
(b) Edward Sapir  (ii) Of Grammatology
(c) Jacques Derrida  (iii) A Course in General Linguistics
(d) Roman Jakobson  (iv) Language
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: Saussure wrote the Course, Sapir wrote Language, Derrida wrote Of Grammatology, and Jakobson wrote the aphasia essay.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q22
items.stem:
Identify the mismatched pair in the
following
where
characters
in
Golding's Lord of the Flies fit the
allegorized pattern of virtues and vices
items.explanation: In the allegorical structure of William Golding's Lord of the Flies (1954), Ralph embodies democratic rationality, Piggy embodies scientific pragmatism, and Simon embodies spiritual innocence. Jack Merridew, who leads the choir boys into savagery and hunting, represents bloodlust and tyranny rather than 'pity'.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q23
items.stem:
Identify the correct statement(s) below :
(a)
"Interlanguage" is a term we owe
to M.A.K. Halliday.

(b)
Interlanguage
develops
an
autonomous and self-contained
grammatical system

(c)
It is a distinct stage in a learner's
progress in the study of a second
language.

(d)
It owes nothing at all either to the
learner's native or target / second
language
items.explanation: In Second Language Acquisition (SLA), 'Interlanguage' denotes a distinct, evolving linguistic stage in a learner's progress toward a second language (c), influenced by both the native and target languages. Although the term was coined by Larry Selinker in 1972, the official UGC key marks both (a) and (c) as correct.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q24
items.stem: A classical influence on Ben Jonson's Volpone is
items.explanation: Ben Jonson's comedy Volpone (1606) draws heavily on the classical Greek Old Comedy of Aristophanes (as well as Roman satirists like Juvenal and Lucian) in its beast-fable caricatures, biting topical satire, and dark, un-romantic comic resolution.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q25
items.stem:
Arrange the following texts chronologically on the basis of the date of publication:
A. Frankenstein by Mary Shelley
B. A Room of One’s Own by Virginia Woolf
C. Maria by Mary Wollstonecraft
D. The Female Eunuch by Germaine Greer
E. The Return of the Soldier by Rebecca West

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The publication timeline begins with Mary Wollstonecraft's Maria: or, The Wrongs of Woman (1798, C), followed by Mary Shelley's Frankenstein (1818, A), Rebecca West's The Return of the Soldier (1918, E), Virginia Woolf's A Room of One's Own (1929, B), and Germaine Greer's The Female Eunuch (1970, D).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q26
items.stem:
Patrick White's Voss is a novel
about
items.explanation: Australian Nobel Laureate Patrick White's historical novel Voss (1957)—inspired by the nineteenth-century Prussian explorer Ludwig Leichhardt—centres on Johann Ulrich Voss's doomed expedition across the vast, unforgiving interior landscape of the Australian desert.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q27
items.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: It is true that there is an analogy between the works of an author and the experiences of his life.
Statement II: The works may be seen as an incomplete translation of the life.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
items.explanation: Both statements are true, drawn from Rene Wellek and Austin Warren's Theory of Literature (Chapter 7, 'Literature and Biography'), which notes that in biographical criticism there is an analogy between an author's works and life experiences, and the works may be viewed as an incomplete translation of the author's life.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q28
items.stem: In which short story does the narrator witness a consumptive young man named Mr. Shaynor recreate “The Eve of St. Agnes” in a trance?
items.explanation: In Kipling's 'Wireless', the chemist's assistant Mr. Shaynor, in a trance, writes lines like Keats's 'The Eve of St. Agnes'.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q29
items.stem:
Who among the following are not part of the Black Aesthetic Movement ?
(A) David Pepper
(B) Stuart Hall
(C) Alan Sinfield
(D) Anthony Appiah
(E) Hazel Carby
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: David Pepper (an environmental geographer) and Alan Sinfield (a British cultural materialist and queer theorist) are not associated with Black cultural criticism or the Black Aesthetic Movement, whereas Stuart Hall, Kwame Anthony Appiah, and Hazel Carby are major theorists of Black diaspora and aesthetics; thus (A) and (C) Only.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q30
items.stem: Who of the following is a Cavalier poet ?
items.explanation: Robert Herrick (1591–1674), author of Hesperides (1648) and 'To the Virgins, to Make Much of Time', was a leading Cavalier poet and one of the 'Sons of Ben' (followers of Ben Jonson). John Donne, George Herbert, and Andrew Marvell are classified as Metaphysical poets.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q31
items.stem:
Match the following :
1. The Sage of Concord
2. The Nun of Amherst
3. Mark Twain
4. Old Possum
5. Emily Dickinson
6. R.W. Emerson
7. T.S. Eliot
8. Samuel L. Clemens
items.explanation: 'The Sage of Concord' is the sobriquet of Ralph Waldo Emerson (1–6); 'The Nun of Amherst' refers to the reclusive poet Emily Dickinson (2–5); Mark Twain is the pen name of Samuel Langhorne Clemens (3–8); and 'Old Possum' was Ezra Pound's nickname for T. S. Eliot (4–7).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q32
items.stem: Which one of the following characters in Shakespeare's Tempest is associated with the Earth ?
items.explanation: In William Shakespeare's The Tempest (1611), Prospero explicitly addresses his enslaved servant Caliban as 'Thou earth, thou!' (Act I, Scene 2), associating Caliban's heavy, physical, and instinctual nature with the element of earth, in contrast to the spirit Ariel, who embodies air and fire.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q33
items.stem:
Which of the following definitions/statements are correct?
A. The term 'nation language' was coined by Derek Walcott
B. 'Poetic justice' is a term invented by Thomas Rymer to convey the idea that evil is punished and virtue is rewarded.
C. The term 'neo-colonialism' was coined by Ngugi Wa Thiong'o.
D. Nihilism is a word invented by Turgenev in his novel Fathers and Sons.
E. Caxton, in preface to Malory's Le Morte d' Arthur listed the nine heroes of late medieval literature
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Thomas Rymer coined 'poetic justice' in The Tragedies of the Last Age Considered (1678, B), Ivan Turgenev popularized 'nihilism' in Fathers and Sons (1862, D), and William Caxton's 1485 preface to Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur discusses the Nine Worthies (E). By contrast, 'nation language' was coined by Kamau Brathwaite (not Derek Walcott) and 'neo-colonialism' by Kwame Nkrumah (not Ngugi); thus B, D, E only.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q34
items.stem:
Which play of Wilde has the sub-
title, A Trivial Comedy for Serious
People ?
items.explanation: Oscar Wilde's farcical masterpiece The Importance of Being Earnest (first performed in February 1895) carries the ironic subtitle A Trivial Comedy for Serious People.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q35
items.stem: Arrange the chronological sequence in which the following works of Richard Hoggart were published: (A) An Imagined Life (B) The Uses of Literacy (C) Higher Education: Demand and Response (D) A Local Habitation (E) A Sort of Clowning Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The publication sequence of Richard Hoggart's works is: The Uses of Literacy (1957), Higher Education: Demand and Response (1980), followed by the three volumes of his autobiography: A Local Habitation (1988), A Sort of Clowning (1990), and An Imagined Life (1992) [(B), (C), (D), (E), (A)].

items.title: Mock #18 · Q36
items.stem: Resistance to slavery created a literature of the abolitionist movement in the last quarter of the eighteenth century in Britain. Such literature included books written by former slaves. Two such writings are Code : I. Mary Robinson II. Olaudah Equiano III. Mary Prince IV. Anne Cromarty Yearsley The right combination according to the code is
items.explanation: Olaudah Equiano (II) and Mary Prince (III) were formerly enslaved writers whose autobiographies—The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano (1789) and The History of Mary Prince (1831)—became landmark British abolitionist texts, whereas Mary Robinson and Ann Yearsley were white British poets.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q37
items.stem:
Assertion (A) : "Tam O' Shanter" by John Clare is about the experience of an ordinary human being and became quite popular during that time.
Reason (R) : John Clare, having suffered bouts of madness, could really feel for the misery of common man.
In the context of the two statements, which of the following is correct ?
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explain (A).
items.explanation: The Official UGC Key marks Option (B), treating both statements as true without causal explanation; note, however, that 'Tam o' Shanter' (1790) was actually written by the Scottish poet Robert Burns rather than the English peasant poet John Clare (1793–1864).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q38
items.stem: What narrative perspective does Chaucer employ in the opening of “The General Prologue”?
items.explanation: Geoffrey Chaucer opens "The General Prologue" to The Canterbury Tales (c. 1387) using a first-person narrator ("Chaucer the Pilgrim"), recounting how he lodged at the Tabard Inn in Southwark ready to embark on his pilgrimage to Canterbury.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q39
items.stem:
What is Gilgamesh ?
(a)
a Babylonian epic poem
(b)
a series of nomic verses
(c)
a classical play
(d)
the story of a harsh ruler
items.explanation: The Epic of Gilgamesh is an ancient Mesopotamian/Babylonian epic poem inscribed on cuneiform clay tablets (a) recounting the heroic exploits, grief, quest for immortality, and harsh reign of Gilgamesh, the tyrannical king of Uruk (d).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q40
items.stem: Which of the following descriptions is NOT true of Peter Carey's The True History of the Kelly Gang ?
options: The novel is dedicated to Edward Kelly's father
It is also about the Bush and the frontier
It has such characters as Edward Kelly, his mother, and his wife
items.explanation: Peter Carey's Booker Prize-winning novel True History of the Kelly Gang (2000) is not dedicated to Ned Kelly's father (it is dedicated to Carey's father, Percival Stanley Carey, while the fictional narrative itself consists of thirteen parcels written by Ned Kelly for his unborn daughter).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q41
items.meta: Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem:
Match the column:
(A) Postmodernism
(B) Psychoanalysis
(C) Mimicry
(D) New Historicism
(I) Jacques Lacan
(II) Stephen Greenblatt
(III) Jean Baudrillard
(IV) Homi Bhabha
items.explanation: Jean Baudrillard is a leading theorist of Postmodernism and hyperreality (A-III); Jacques Lacan reformulated Psychoanalysis using linguistic structures (B-I); Homi Bhabha theorized postcolonial Mimicry in The Location of Culture (C-IV); and Stephen Greenblatt pioneered New Historicism (D-II).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q42
items.stem:
"And if no peece of chronicle we
prove,

We'll build in ________ pretty
roomes."
items.explanation: In John Donne's metaphysical poem "The Canonization" (1633), the speaker declares that even if their love is unfit for grand historical chronicles, they will "build in sonnets pretty rooms," playing on the Italian word stanza (meaning "room").

items.title: Mock #18 · Q43
items.stem:
Which of the following parameters are emphasised in MLA Handbook's (9th Edition) chapter titled, "Principles of Inclusive Language"?
A. Avoid negatively judging other's experiences.
B. Use a dictionary to check for offensive terms.
C. Extensive use of pronouns.
D. Any format for capitalization and styling.
E. Make references to identity relevant sources.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: The MLA Handbook (9th edition) section 'Principles of Inclusive Language' advises writers to avoid negatively judging others' experiences (A), consult an up-to-date dictionary to check whether terms are offensive (B), and make references to identity only when relevant to the context (E), matching A, B and E only.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q44
items.stem:
A poet laureate said “I do not think that since Shakespeare there has been such a aster of
the English language as I.” Who is the poet ?
items.explanation: Alfred Lord Tennyson, Victorian Poet Laureate from 1850 until his death in 1892, famously boasted of his supreme auditory and verbal craft: 'I do not think that since Shakespeare there has been such a master of the English language as I.'

items.title: Mock #18 · Q45
items.stem: What is the correct order of publication of the novels of Charles Dickens? (A) Great Expectations (B) Hard Times (C) Oliver Twist (D) David Copperfield (E) A Tale of Two Cities Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The chronological publication order of Charles Dickens's novels is: Oliver Twist (1837-1839), David Copperfield (1849-1850), Hard Times (1854), A Tale of Two Cities (1859), and Great Expectations (1860-1861) [(C), (D), (B), (E), (A)].

items.title: Mock #18 · Q46
items.stem: The phrase “darkness visible” (Paradise Lost, 1.63) is an example of __________.
items.explanation: In Milton's Paradise Lost (1.63), the description of Hell's flames that provide 'No light, but rather darkness visible' is a classic oxymoron, juxtaposing two contradictory sensory ideas to convey infernal gloom.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q47
items.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Comparative Literature is a study of different cultures, nations and genres, and it explores the inherent relationship between literature and other forms of cultural exploration.
Statement II: In the study of literature and culture, the importance of methodology is secondary.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
items.explanation: Comparative Literature examines literature across national, linguistic, and disciplinary boundaries (Statement I is true), but rigorous theoretical methodology is central—never secondary—to comparative literary and cultural studies (Statement II is false).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q48
items.stem:
Which of the following can be best
described as : (i) the first statement of
Bernard Shaw's idea of Life Force; (ii)
a play dealing with a woman's pursuit
of her mate; and (iii) a play whose
third act called "Don Juan in Hell" is
both unconventional and hilarious ?
items.explanation: George Bernard Shaw's play Man and Superman: A Comedy and a Philosophy (1903) introduces his concept of the creative 'Life Force', depicts Ann Whitefield's determined pursuit of John Tanner, and includes the famous philosophical dream interlude 'Don Juan in Hell' as Act III.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q49
items.stem:
Identify the plays that John Fletcher wrote in collaboration with Francis Beaumont:
A. The Faithful Shepherdess
B. The Loyal Subject
C. Cupid's Revenge
D. The Pilgrim
E. The Maid's Tragedy
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Cupid's Revenge (C, c. 1607–08) and The Maid's Tragedy (E, c. 1609–11) were co-written by John Fletcher and Francis Beaumont, whereas The Faithful Shepherdess (1608), The Loyal Subject (1618), and The Pilgrim (1621) were solo plays by Fletcher; thus C and E only.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q50
items.stem: Who among the following called the ‘Poetasters’, “The rhyming friends”?
items.explanation: Horace mocked second-rate versifiers (poetasters) in his Satires and Epistles.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q51
items.stem:
Match List I with List II
List I (Word Borrowed) – List II (Source Language)
(a) caste  (i) Norse
(b) beef  (ii) German
(c) blunder  (iii) Portuguese
(d) flak  (iv) French
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: 'Caste' is from Portuguese, 'beef' from French, 'blunder' from Norse, and 'flak' from German (Fliegerabwehrkanone).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q52
items.stem: Who among the following has written the essay, "The Indian Jugglers" ?
items.explanation: Romantic essayist William Hazlitt wrote 'The Indian Jugglers' (published in Table-Talk, 1821), using the astonishing physical dexterity of an Indian juggler in London to meditate on the difference between mechanical skill and imaginative artistic genius.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q53
items.meta: Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem: Identify the correct option in Julia Kristeva's definition of 'chora': (A) Liminal Space (B) Space of the marginalised (C) Non-expressive totality created by the bodily drives (D) The chora has no fixed identity (E) It precedes the linguistic sign Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In Revolution in Poetic Language (1974), Julia Kristeva adopts Plato's concept of the 'chora' to designate the pre-Oedipal semiotic realm: a dynamic, non-expressive totality produced by instinctual bodily drives (C) that lacks unified or fixed spatial identity (D) and precedes the symbolic linguistic sign and syntax (E).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q54
items.stem: Identify the term among the following which does not relate to a movement in art or literature.
items.explanation: Empiricism is a philosophical epistemological theory associated with Locke, Berkeley, and Hume asserting that knowledge derives from sensory experience, whereas Cubism, Expressionism, and Surrealism are prominent artistic and literary movements of the early twentieth century.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q55
items.stem:
Arrange the following in the chronological order of their publication :
(A) Past and Present
(B) Leviathan
(C) Unto This Last
(D) The Life of Samuel Johnson
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: Leviathan (1651), Boswell's Life of Johnson (1791), Carlyle's Past and Present (1843), Ruskin's Unto This Last (1860).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q56
items.stem: Which one of the following correctly describes the meaning of Macbeth's words '... life is but a walking shadow'?
options: Life is just devoid of light
Life is just devoid of stability
Life is just devoid of spirit
Life is just devoid of substance
items.explanation: A shadow has no substance, so Macbeth calls life empty and without real meaning.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q57
items.stem:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as
Reason R

Assertion A: The introduction of English in India was primarily for the benefit and
consolidation of British power.

Reason R: English catered to the social and economic aspirations of the emerging middle
class and urban elites in India.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
Ais false but R is true
items.explanation: Both statements are historically true: colonial policies like Macaulay's Minute of 1835 introduced English primarily to consolidate British administrative control, and English education simultaneously served the economic and social mobility of India's emerging urban middle class. However, Indian middle-class aspirations were a consequence rather than the primary cause of British imperial policy.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q58
items.stem: According to Ferdinand de Saussure, what is the minimum number necessary to complete the speaking-circuit?
items.explanation: In *Course in General Linguistics* (1916), Ferdinand de Saussure establishes that completing the communicative speaking-circuit (*le circuit de la parole*) requires a minimum of two interacting individuals (a speaker and a listener).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q59

B. Dostoevsky
C. Mallarme

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Australian poet A.D. Hope's collection A Book of Answers (1978) features poetic dialogues with canonical writers including Leo Tolstoy ('Country Places: An Epistle to Leo Tolstoy'), Stéphane Mallarmé, and Fyodor Dostoevsky (keyed as A and C only).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q60
items.stem: "With all the eagerness to know the truths of life, she retained very childlike ideas about marriage … the really delightful marriage must be that when your husband was a sort of a father, and could even teach you Hebrew, if you wished it." She is the protagonist in one of George Eliot's novels. Who is she ?
items.explanation: This passage from Chapter 1 of George Eliot's Middlemarch (1871–72) describes the idealistic protagonist Dorothea Brooke. Seeking lofty intellectual and spiritual purpose, she naively marries the pedantic, aging scholar Rev. Edward Casaubon, imagining him as a fatherly sage.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q62
items.stem:
Christopher Marlowe was one of the first major writers to affirm what can be identified as a
clearly homosexual sensibility.  Which drama of his deals with it ?
items.explanation: Christopher Marlowe's historical tragedy Edward II (c. 1592) is recognized as one of the earliest English plays to openly explore homosexual desire and aristocratic homoerotic passion through King Edward's devotion to Piers Gaveston.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q63
items.stem:
According to Stuart Hall which of these is generally accepted to be true of Cultural Studies as it was practised at the University of Birmingham in the UK?

A. It sought to strengthen the barrier between high culture and low culture
B. It sought to privilege the study of the text at the cost of context
C. It could accommodate the study of the lives of working class people
D. It sought to promote readings based on social and political contexts
E. It was essentially apolitical

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Stuart Hall highlighted that Cultural Studies at the Birmingham Centre for Contemporary Cultural Studies (CCCS) dismantled the elitist divide to validate working-class cultural life (C) and insisted on historicizing cultural practices within concrete socio-political structures (D).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q64
items.stem: Which of the following works cannot be categorised under postcolonial theory ?
items.explanation: Edward Said's Orientalism (1978), Homi K. Bhabha's edited volume Nation and Narration (1990), and Robert J. C. Young's White Mythologies (1990) are foundational texts of postcolonial theory, whereas Michel Foucault's Discipline and Punish (1975) is a post-structuralist history of the modern penal system.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q65

B. Sons and Lovers

C. Mrs Dalloway

D. A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: D. H. Lawrence's Sons and Lovers (B) was published in 1913, followed by James Joyce's A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (D) in 1916. Aldous Huxley's debut country-house satire Crome Yellow (A) appeared in 1921, and Virginia Woolf's modernist novel Mrs Dalloway (C) was published in 1925.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q66
items.stem:
In which play do we see a reworking
of E.M.Forster's A Passage to India
as a camaeo ?
items.explanation: Tom Stoppard's play Indian Ink (1995) alternates between 1930 colonial India and 1980s England, pastiching and reworking motifs of Anglo-Indian cross-cultural encounter from E. M. Forster's A Passage to India (1924).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q67
items.stem:
Which among the following is not true about E.P. Thompson's The Making of the Working Class?

A. Studies the development of working class consciousness

B. Defines class as a relationship not as a social structure

C. It is the first systematic study of the history of working class

D. It critiques Virginia Woolf's A Room of One's Own

E. Reinforces the idea that race and ethnicity are the forms of collective identity

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Statements D and E are false: E.P. Thompson's The Making of the English Working Class (1963) concentrates on English artisans and working-class people between 1780 and 1832, making no critique of Virginia Woolf's feminist essay A Room of One's Own (1929) and focusing primarily on socio-economic class rather than race or ethnicity.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q68
items.stem: Which of these themes best sums up the preoccupation of most of Vijay Tendulkar's plays?
items.explanation: Marathi playwright Vijay Tendulkar's major plays—including Silence! The Court Is in Session (1967), Sakharam Binder (1972), and Ghashiram Kotwal (1972)—centrally interrogate the brutal workings of political, patriarchal, and institutional power.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q69
items.stem: Match List - I with List - II. List - I (Character) List - II (Novel) (A) Sethe (I) The Handmaid's Tale (B) Okonkwo (II) Beloved (C) Offred (III) Things Fall Apart (D) Winston Smith (IV) Nineteen Eighty-Four Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The correct character-to-novel pairings are: Sethe is the runaway slave protagonist in Toni Morrison's Beloved (1987) [(A)-(II)]; Okonkwo is the tragic Igbo warrior in Chinua Achebe's Things Fall Apart (1958) [(B)-(III)]; Offred is the narrator-handmaid in Margaret Atwood's The Handmaid's Tale (1985) [(C)-(I)]; and Winston Smith is the dissident outer-party worker in George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four (1949) [(D)-(IV)].

items.title: Mock #18 · Q70

items.explanation: Milton opens Book I of Paradise Lost with a magnificent 16-line periodic sentence invocation ('Of Man's First Disobedience... Sing Heav'nly Muse...') that builds to line 16 ('Things unattempted yet in prose or rhyme').

items.title: Mock #18 · Q71

items.explanation: Arnold Bennett (B), H.G. Wells (C), and E.M. Forster (D) are major novelists of the Edwardian era (1901–1910/1914), whereas George Eliot (1819–1880) and Robert Louis Stevenson (1850–1894) were Victorian novelists.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q72
items.stem: “The just man justices.” What kind of foregrounding do you find in the above lines ?
items.explanation: In Gerard Manley Hopkins's sonnet "As Kingfishers Catch Fire," the clause "The just man justices" turns the adjective/noun "just" into a verb ("justices"), creating syntactic (and semantic) foregrounding; UGC accepted both (A) and (B).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q73
items.stem: What is the correct chronological sequence of the following ?
options: Tristram Shandy, Moll Flanders, Pamela, Joseph Andrews
Joseph Andrews, Tristram Shandy, Pamela, Moll Flanders
Moll Flanders, Pamela, Joseph Andrews, Tristram Shandy
Pamela, Moll Flanders, Joseph Andrews, Tristram Shandy
items.explanation: The correct chronological order of these eighteenth-century English novels is Daniel Defoe's Moll Flanders (1722), Samuel Richardson's Pamela (1740), Henry Fielding's Joseph Andrews (1742), and Laurence Sterne's Tristram Shandy (1759–1767).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q74
items.stem:

the play The Knight of the Burning Pestle
items.explanation: In Francis Beaumont's metadramatic burlesque comedy The Knight of the Burning Pestle (c. 1607), a London Citizen (a grocer) and his Wife interrupt the stage performance and insist that their apprentice, Rafe (Ralph), take a leading role as a grocer-errant with a burning pestle on his shield.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q75
items.stem: Which of the following is true about Tennessee Williams' A Street Car Named Desire? (A) It is set in New Orleans. (B) The protagonist is a Mississippi landowner. (C) It ends with Blanche's defeat and departure. (D) Tom Wingfield is the narrator. (E) Laura and Stella are cousins. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Tennessee Williams's A Streetcar Named Desire (1947) is set in the French Quarter of New Orleans [(A)] and concludes with Blanche DuBois's tragic mental collapse and removal to an asylum [(C)]. Statements (B), (D), and (E) are false because Stanley is a factory worker, Blanche lost the Belle Reve estate, and Tom and Laura Wingfield are characters from Williams's The Glass Menagerie.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q76
items.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT TRUE regarding the poems of Derek Walcott ?
options: is poem “Goats and Monkeys” has an epigraph from Shakespeare’s Othello
In “The Sadhu of Couva” Walcott refers to Diwali, anuman and the Ramayana
In “A Far Cry From Africa” Walcott depicts his divided loyalties in the context of the Changuna Uprising
Walcott has written a poem entitled “Jean Rhys”
items.explanation: Derek Walcott's famous poem 'A Far Cry from Africa' (In a Green Night, 1962) explores his divided Caribbean-British-African identity against the historical backdrop of the Mau Mau Uprising in 1950s Kenya, NOT the fictional 'Changuna Uprising'.

A. Krishnaswamy authored The Flute of Krishna (1950) (D-III). This gives A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q78
items.stem: "For nature then The courser pleasures of my boyish days, And their glad animal movements all gone by To me was all in all". In these lines from "Tintern Abbey Revisited", Wordsworth is talking about
options: the second stage in his relationship with Nature
the third stage in his relationship with Nature
both the first and second stages in his relationship with Nature
the first stage in his relationship with Nature
items.explanation: In William Wordsworth's 'Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey' (1798), 'the coarser pleasures of my boyish days, / And their glad animal movements' refer to the first, purely physical and unreflective boyhood stage of his relationship with Nature.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q79

items.explanation: The chronological order of publication is Thomas Carlyle's The French Revolution (1837), Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species (1859), John Ruskin's Unto This Last (1860 in Cornhill / 1862), Walter Pater's Studies in the History of the Renaissance (1873), and John Richard Green's The Making of England (1881).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q80
items.stem:
"The Lost Generation" is a name applied to the disillusioned intellectuals and aesthetes
of the years following the First World War. Who called them "The Lost Generation" ?
items.explanation: American modernist writer Gertrude Stein coined and popularized the phrase 'You are all a lost generation' in Paris (adapting a remark by a French garage owner), which Ernest Hemingway famously used as an epigraph to his 1926 novel The Sun Also Rises.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q81
items.stem:

LIST-I (Archetype symbols) | LIST-II (Symbolic Meanings)
A. The sea | I. Creative Energy
B. Rivers | II. Wisdom
C. Sun | III. The mother of all life
D. Serpent | IV. Death and rebirth
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In archetypal criticism (as summarized in Guerin's A Handbook of Critical Approaches to Literature), the sea symbolizes the mother of all life and the unconscious (A-III), rivers symbolize death and rebirth or the flowing of time (B-IV), the sun represents creative energy and consciousness (C-I), and the serpent embodies primal energy and hidden wisdom (D-II).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q82
items.stem: Northanger Abbey is a parody of the _______ romance
items.explanation: Jane Austen's novel Northanger Abbey (completed 1803, published posthumously in 1817) is a satirical parody of late eighteenth-century Gothic romances, particularly Ann Radcliffe's The Mysteries of Udolpho (1794), which overstimulate the imagination of its young heroine Catherine Morland.

Wells's The Time Machine (1895, D), Rudyard Kipling's Kim (1901, B), Arnold Bennett's The Old Wives' Tale (1908, C), and James Joyce's A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (1916, E), giving A, D, B, C, E.

Gandhi's The Story of My Experiments with Truth (1927), and Sharankumar Limbale's The Outcaste: Akkarmashi (1984) are all autobiographies.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q88

items.explanation: Thomas Chatterton (1752–1770), famous for his pseudo-medieval 'Rowley' poems attributed to an imaginary 15th-century monk, died by arsenic poisoning in a London garret at age seventeen after living close to starvation. Wordsworth later memorialized him in 'Resolution and Independence' as 'the marvellous Boy.'

items.title: Mock #18 · Q90

items.explanation: In Dickens's Dombey and Son the railway train is the central symbol of industrial modernity and death (i-2); in Hardy's The Return of the Native Egdon Heath dominates the narrative (ii-3); in Dickens's Bleak House the London fog symbolizes the obfuscation of the Court of Chancery (iii-1); and in Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles mist shrouds key scenes such as the Chase (iv-4).

items.title: Mock #18 · Q91
items.stem:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:
[T]he aim of all solitude...is the same: to live more at leisure and at one's ease. But people do not always look for the right
way. Often they think they have left business, and they have only changed it. There is scarcely less trouble in governing a
family than in governing an entire state: whatever the mind is wrapped up in it, it is all wrapped up in it, and domestic
occupations are no less importunate for being less important. Furthermore, by getting rid of the court and the marketplace
we do not get rid of the principal worries of our life....Ambition, avarice, irresolution, fear and lust do not leave us when
we change our country....They often follow us even into the cloisters and schools of philosophy. Neither deserts, nor rocky
caves, nor hair shirts, nor fastings will free us of them.
                                                              --  Michel de Montaigne, "Of solitude"
Which of the following best captures the theme of the passage?
options: The court and the marketplace must be got rid of
Try what one may, no one can ever be at ease
Ruling a state is easier than managing a family
Solitude is one condition of peace with one self
items.explanation: In his essay 'Of Solitude' (Essais, Book I, Chapter 39), Michel de Montaigne argues that genuine solitude is not mere physical withdrawal from court or marketplace, but achieving inner peace and self-sufficiency within one's own mind.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q94
items.stem:
Read the following poem and answer the questions that follow:

A Prayer for Old Age
God guard me from those thoughts men think
In the mind alone;
He that sings a lasting song
Thinks in a marrow-bone;

From all that makes a wise old man
That can be praised of all;
O what am I that I should not seem
For the song's sake a fool?

I pray--for fashion's word is out
And prayer comes round again --
That I may seem, though I die old,
A foolish, passionate man.
                                                            - W.B.Yeats

Thoughts true for all time are:
items.explanation: In W.B. Yeats's poem 'A Prayer for Old Age' (1934), the lines 'He that sings a lasting song / Thinks in a marrow-bone' mean that enduring poetic truths are felt viscerally deep inside the self rather than in abstract intellect alone.

items.explanation: This famous passage from Chapter 1 of Charles Dickens's Dombey and Son (1848) uses biting sarcasm and ironic hyperbole to satirize Mr. Paul Dombey's mercantile arrogance in viewing the entire universe as existing solely for his firm.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q98
items.meta: Unit IV / Unit VIII: Prose & Criticism
items.stem:
Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow:
The earth was made for Dombey and Son to trade in, and the sun and moon were made to give them light. Rivers and
seas were formed to float their ships; rainbows gave them promise of fair weather; winds blew for or against their
enterprises; stars and planets circled in their orbits, to preserve inviolate a system of which they were the centre.

Common abbreviations took new meanings in his eyes, and had sole reference to them: A. D. had no concern with
anno Domini, but stood for anno Dombey-and Son.
                                 - Charles Dickens, Dombey and Son

What is the 'system' of which Dombey and Son were the centre?
items.explanation: In Mr. Dombey's egoistic worldview, the solar and natural workings of the cosmos revolve solely to preserve his family shipping enterprise, 'Dombey and Son,' as the center of existence.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q99
items.meta: Unit IV / Unit VIII: Prose & Criticism
items.stem:
Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow:

Is man no more than this? Consider him well. Thou ow'st the worm no silk, the beast no hide, the sheep no wool, the
cat no perfume. --- Ha! here's three on's are sophisticated. Thou art the thing itself; unaccommodated man is no more
than such a poor, bare, forked animal as thou art.
                                                            - Shakespeare, King Lear
'Is man no more than this?' means:
options: Man is not as well endowed as some other animals
Man is far more than what he seems to be
As an animal, man is a superior animal
items.explanation: In Act 3, Scene 4 of Shakespeare's King Lear, Lear looks at the half-naked Edgar ('Poor Tom') on the stormy heath and realizes that natural, 'unaccommodated man' is a frail, bare creature less naturally endowed with protective coverings than animals.

items.title: Mock #18 · Q100
items.meta: Unit IV / Unit VIII: Prose & Criticism
items.stem:
Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow:
Is man no more than this? Consider him well. Thou ow'st the worm no silk, the beast no hide, the sheep no wool, the
cat no perfume. --- Ha! here's three on's are sophisticated. Thou art the thing itself; unaccommodated man is no more
than such a poor, bare, forked animal as thou art.
                                                            - Shakespeare, King Lear
Which one of the following best captures what Shakespeare means?
options: Man just uses what animals possess
Animals unlike man are more complex
items.explanation: By declaring 'Thou ow'st the worm no silk, the beast no hide, the sheep no wool, the cat no perfume,' Lear recognizes that civilized humans merely borrow and use external coverings that naturally belong to animals.
